title: Continuatio Fragmentorum ex Adversariis mathematicis depromptorum

deep.reconstruction:
The page has two independent pieces.

(1) Corollary to the theorem on the previous page, S(1) = 3π²/32.
- Put h_n = Σ_{k=0}^{n} (-1)^k/(2k+1) and S(x) = Σ_n (-1)^n h_n x^{2n+1}/(2n+1).
- Then S'(x) = Σ_n (-1)^n h_n x^{2n}.
- Euler collects by k: Σ_k [(-1)^k/(2k+1)] Σ_{n≥k} (-1)^n x^{2n} = Σ_k x^{2k}/(2k+1) · 1/(1+x²).
- Hence S'(x) = artanh(x)/(x(1+x²)), i.e. (1/(x(1+xx)))∫dx/(1-xx).
- Using 1/(x(1+x²)) = 1/x − x/(1+x²) gives S = ∫(dx/x)·artanh x − ∫ x·artanh x/(1+x²) dx.
- The first term is Legendre's chi function χ₂(x) = Σ x^{2k+1}/(2k+1)², which equals π²/8 at x = 1.
- With S(1) = 3π²/32 he concludes ∫₀¹ x·artanh(x)/(1+x²) dx = π²/32.
- He adds that he does not see how to obtain this value directly.

(2) Problem: transform the prime series s = 1/3 − 1/5 + 1/7 + 1/11 − 1/13 − … = −Σ_{p odd} χ₄(p)/p into a convergent series, where χ₄ is the non-principal character mod 4.
- First product: the Euler product L(1,χ₄) = π/4 = Π p/(p−χ₄(p)) gives π/4 · 4/3 · 4/5 · 8/7 · 12/11 · 12/13 … = 1.
- With partial products P_k (P_0 = π/4, P_k → 1) one has P_k − P_{k−1} = −χ(p_k)P_{k−1}/p_k.
- Therefore −χ(p_k)/p_k = (P_k − P_{k−1}) − (χ(p_k)/p_k)(1 − P_{k−1}).
- Summing telescopes to s = 1 − π/4 + Σ_k (−χ(p_k)/p_k)(1 − P_{k−1}). This reproduces Euler's terms exactly: (1/3)(1 − π/4), (1/5)(4/3·π/4 − 1), (1/7)(1 − 16/15·π/4), and so on.
- Second product: Π_{p odd}(1 + χ₄(p)/p) = L(1,χ₄)/Π(1 − p⁻²)⁻¹ = (π/4)/(π²/8) = 2/π. This is (π/2)·2/3·6/5·6/7·10/11·14/13 … = 1.
- The same telescoping with Q_k gives s = π/2 − 1 − Σ (χ(p_k)/p_k)(1 − Q_{k−1}). This again matches all printed terms.
- In both series each 1/p is multiplied by a factor tending to 0, which is what Euler means by 'convergent'.
- The page ends by opening a theorem with q = π/4. The next page has the recursion for Dirichlet β and λ values (Euler/tangent numbers), and then takes logarithms of the quotient of the two products — the route of E596 to the numerical value s ≈ 0.33498.
errors: No real errors; all intermediate formulas check (signs of the 'secundi/tertii' groups, the partial fractions, and every term of both prime series).
The integral value is correct. Known integrals give ∫₀¹ x ln(1+x)/(1+x²)dx = π²/96 + (ln2)²/8 and ∫₀¹ x ln(1−x)/(1+x²)dx = (ln2)²/8 − 5π²/96. Half their difference is π²/32.
Gaps typical of Euler, none fatal:
– He sets x = 1 at the boundary, which needs Abel's theorem.
– He assumes the prime series converges; its convergence is actually equivalent to PNT-strength information for arithmetic progressions.
– 'valde convergunt' is overstated. The factors 1 − P_{k−1} are only tails of Σχ(p)/p, which decay roughly like 1/log p unconditionally, so the acceleration is modest.

ideas.what: Generating-function treatment of S(x) = Σ (-1)^n h_n x^{2n+1}/(2n+1) with partial Leibniz sums h_n, reducing it to artanh and the chi function
ideas.modern_name: Generating functions of Euler-type (alternating harmonic) sums; Legendre chi function χ₂
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (Euler sums); χ₂ named after Legendre
ideas.where_published: Similar manipulations appear in Euler's papers on sums of products of harmonic-type numbers (e.g. E477); this specific one only here (Opera postuma 1862)

ideas.what: Evaluation ∫₀¹ x·artanh(x)/(1+x²) dx = π²/32, obtained indirectly
ideas.usually_credited_to: Appears in integral tables; no specific attribution

ideas.what: Euler products for L(1,χ₄) = π/4 and Π(1+χ₄(p)/p) = 2/π
ideas.modern_name: Euler product for the Dirichlet L-function L(s,χ₄) at s = 1
ideas.where_published: Introductio in analysin infinitorum (E101), vol. I ch. 15; E596

ideas.what: Telescoping a convergent infinite product into a series that accelerates a prime sum: Σ a_k = (lim P − P₀) + Σ a_k(1 − P_{k−1})
ideas.modern_name: Series acceleration for prime sums via partial Euler products
ideas.where_published: E596 treats the same series s, but mainly via logarithms and odd-power prime sums; whether this telescoped form is there is unsure

ideas.what: The prime series Σ ±1/p with signs by residue mod 4
ideas.modern_name: Σ_p χ₄(p)/p (Mertens-type constant for primes in progressions mod 4)
ideas.where_published: E596 'De summa seriei ex numeris primis formata 1/3 − 1/5 + 1/7 + 1/11 − …'

missed.claim: Euler states he cannot derive ∫ x dx/(1+xx) · ∫ dx/(1−xx) = π²/32 directly. The substitution x = (1−t)/(1+t) does it at once. It turns the integral into −½∫₀¹ ln t [1/(1+t) − t/(1+t²)] dt = −½(−π²/12 + π²/48) = π²/32, using only integrals Euler himself knew.
missed.quote: quem valorem non video quomodo directe erui posset
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest only: an open question Euler raised that is closed by an elementary Landen-type substitution.

missed.claim: A draft of the E596 problem, using a product-telescoping acceleration of Σ χ₄(p)/p built from two different Euler products. This may differ from the logarithmic method of the published paper (unsure).
missed.quote: Hoc duplici modo fieri potest. Cum enim primo sit productum π/4·4/3·4/5·8/7… = 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of interest for the genesis of E596. Mathematically it is superseded by the Möbius–log-L method for computing prime sums.

deep.surprise_reason: Both results are correct, but they are routine or anticipate the published E596. The integral is a standard table value with a short direct proof. The telescoping acceleration is a minor, possibly unrecorded, variant of known Euler material.
transcription_corrections: Transcription agrees with the image; no substantive corrections needed.
